title: ‘What a Waste of Time,’ ‘Played His Cards Perfectly’ — Buccaneers World Split As Vita Vea Drama Ends With Massive $30M Extension
description: Vita Vea is not going anywhere. He’s spent his entire career with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and will stay in pewter for the time being.
fullText:
Vita Vea is not going anywhere. He's spent his entire career with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and will stay in pewter for the time being.

After Vea requested a trade earlier in training camp, a potential exit was in the cards. But Vea and Tampa Bay were able to reach an agreement on a contract to keep Vea around through the 2027 season. Buccaneers fans can take a breath as the saga is over, but not everyone is pleased with the outcome.

Vea wanted to be paid what he thought he deserved, and he got it. Vea got himself a one-year, $30 million extension from Tampa Bay that will go through the 2027 season.

While the extension is worth one year and $30 million, some of the new money will be tacked on to the $18 million that Vea was slated to earn in the 2026 season. According to Buccaneers insider Rick Stroud, Vea will earn an additional $6 million, bringing his 2026 total to $24 million. He will earn that same amount for the 2027 season.

Vea is dominant in the trenches, but as he gets older, the price gets hefty. One Buccaneers fan isn't too thrilled with Tampa Bay giving in to Vea's demands.

"What a waste of time. I blame this on [Ndamukong] Suh and Vita. Being smart about business requires knowing the market. Vita is good. But his asset loss is in his age. It is a part of the game. Vita better play his ass off. He acted like he needed a three year deal when we all know: NO!" said one fan.

It's safe to say that the Buccaneers faithful aren't in harmony over this extension, with some pumped to see the big man back in the Tampa Bay trenches.

"So happy!! He's so important to this defense,"said one fan.

Whether Buccaneers fans love it or hate it, Vea is here to stay for the next two seasons, and he will be thrilled with his new contract.

"Wow. Vita played his cards perfectly. Big fella got PAID! Good for him, good on the Bucs for shelling out that deserved cash since this is his last season with Tampa," said one fan.

One fan even admitted they were wrong to think a trade request was the wrong move, as Vea ended up getting what he wanted.

"Well I think he made the right call to get a deal done. I thought a hold out was not good advice. He wanted his money and he got it. Maybe can't knock him too much," said one fan.

The Buccaneers fans aren't forgetting what happened last season, though. Their late-season collapse has left a bad taste in many mouths, and the pressure is on the coaching staff, front office, and the owners. Although the owners forked up the money for Vea, some fans aren't letting them off the hook.

"This is the owners giving [Todd] Bowles no excuses. Still a prove it year for players and coaches. Vea included," said one fan.

There needs to be progress for the Buccaneers. Winning the division in a weak NFC South might not cut it for the Buccaneers faithful after missing the playoffs last year, as they've experienced winning the division and getting bounced quickly from the playoffs. They're waiting for a breakthrough and getting impatient with this post-Tom Brady crew. It's now or never for Tampa Bay, and Vea will have to be a big part of this team's success with his new extension.

title: Stephanie White Gives Kelsey Mitchell Update After Fever Star Exits Win Over Tempo
description: Indiana Fever coach Stephanie White provided an update on Kelsey Mitchell after she exited a 101-95 win over the Toronto Tempo after scoring 29 points.
fullText:
The Indiana Fever earned their 24th win of the season against the Toronto Tempo on Aug. 18 with guard Kelsey Mitchell exiting the game due to overheating.

Indiana defeated Toronto 101-95, but the win was overshadowed by Mitchell sitting out the fourth quarter. She scored 29 points on 11 of 16 shooting from the field and tied the WNBA record for most consecutive 20+ point games.

The Ohio State product finished with more than 20 points for the 20th straight contest. With the regular season winding down, there should be no concern about Mitchell, according to head coach Stephanie White.

According to Tony East, the Fever guard has no major concerns.

"Seems like she just got overheated," White said.

"It was the second-straight hot game environment for the Fever," White added.

Mitchell was drafted to the Fever with the second pick in the 2018 WNBA Draft. She has played all nine seasons with the franchise. Since being drafted, the franchise has only made the postseason twice, in 2024 and 2025.

Indiana is on track to reach the postseason for the third consecutive season. The 5-foot-8 guard is averaging 24.3 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 2.6 assists while shooting 44.3% from three-point range.

Mitchell is shooting a career-high 50.7% from the field and has played in all 36 games for the Fever this season.

Throughout the season, Indiana has faced off-court issues but has remained focused on the season. During the Aug. 16 contest between the Atlanta Dream and Indiana Fever, women were reportedly asked to cover their shirts because of messages on them. 

 The WNBA stated that fans should not have been asked to cover their shirts, according to the Associated Press. This followed guard Sophie Cunningham's comments on transgender athletes this season.

Fever head coach White spoke up after the controversial foul from forward Alyssa Thomas on guard Caitlin Clark earlier in the season. White also commented on the foul committed by Chicago Sky guard DiJonai Carrington on Cunningham on Aug. 8.

Clark has also been the subject of political conversation as NBA commissioner Adam Silver called her a "political football." Despite the adversity that Indiana has experienced this season, they are trending upward.

Indiana is 24-12 on the season and is third in league standings after defeating the Toronto Tempo on Aug. 19.

The Fever will face the Dallas Wings next on Aug. 20 at 8 p.m. ET on Prime Video. Mitchell was listed as probable on the injury report ahead of that matchup.

title: The Celtics Have a Mitchell Robinson Problem They Have to Address
description: The Celtics are about to get a taste of their own medicine.
fullText:
The Celtics Have a Mitchell Robinson Problem They Have to Address originally appeared on NESN. 

The prospect of Mitchell Robinson in the Celtics' rotation next season is an exciting thought.

Robinson adds depth to Boston's roster, giving them a consistent rebounder and defender, among several other skills he possesses.

However, he has one major weakness that the Celtics are well aware of, and now Boston will have to find a way to help Robinson fix it.

The Celtics and Joe Mazzulla have been known to use the 'hack-a-Shaq' method in recent seasons, and Mitchell Robinson was one of the frequent victims of this tactic when he was with the Knicks.

The Celtics would intentionally foul Robinson, knowing he was a bad free-throw shooter.

MORE: Neemias Queta Has Message For Celtics Doubters Ahead of 2026-27 NBA Season

Doing this meant they preferred, towards the end of quarters, the gamble of putting Robinson at the line for two shots, rather than risking letting up points in another way.

The method did work, but it slowed the pace of the game down dramatically, and could only really be done for so long before certain players accumulated too many fouls.

It's definitely a strategic move, but if Robinson continues to show he can't hit free throws at a respectable rate, teams will continue to employ the intentional foul tactic.

MORE: Celtics Owner Bill Chisholm Explains How Boston Could Get a New Arena

The Celtics now may have to deal with the tactic that they've used the most in the past, and it could be problematic for them if Robinson doesn't improve his FT%.

Even with this tactic not being used intentionally, it's not good in general that he is a poor free-throw shooter, as missed free throws accumulating throughout a game will come back to hurt the Celtics.

Robinson shot a career-worst 40.8% at the free-throw line this past season. It wouldn't be fair to expect him to double that, but Boston will really need to work with him to get that percentage back up into at least the mid-to-high 60% range.

title: Lake Travis High football cancels season opener after death of Odin Hensley
description: Lake Travis High School football canceled its season opener on Aug. 28 following the death of senior OL Odin Hensley on Aug. 13.
fullText:
Business will not be as usual for Lake Travis High School football during Week 1 of the 2026 Texas high school football season.

According to a tweet from the Cavaliers' football account on X (formerly Twitter), the team's season opener against Dripping Springs on Friday, Aug. 28, has been canceled. That includes varsity, sub-varsity and freshman games.

The decision to cancel the game comes following the death of senior offensive lineman Odin Hensley Hensley died following a cardiac arrest episode on Aug. 12 at Dell Children's Hospital. Hensley experienced a "serious medical emergency" two days prior at a team practice.

"The past two weeks have been incredibly difficult for everyone involved," head coach Hank Carter wrote in the tweet. "After careful consideration and with the physical and mental safety of our players and staff as our top priority, we have made the decision to cancel our football games against Dripping Springs next week."

Carter left the door open for a potential controlled scrimmage instead of the game, but he said a decision won't be made until the next couple of days over the weekend.

Following the medical episode, Hensley was flown to Travis County Star Flight to Dell Children's Medical Center on Aug. 11.

A GoFundMe was set up to help his family and has raised over $208,000 as of Wednesday, Aug. 19.

Hensley will be honored with a "celebration of life" on Saturday, Aug. 22 at 2 p.m. at the Austin Ridge Bible Church.

Lake Travis is now scheduled to kick off its season against Weiss Sept. 4 at The Pfield in Pflugerville, Texas.

title: Cleveland Cavaliers acquire Peyton Watson, an NBA champ with Nuggets
description: The Cleveland Cavaliers shifted to Peyton Watson after LeBron James decided to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers. What to know about the move.
fullText:
Weeks after losing the LeBron James sweepstakes, the Cavaliers are securing a fallback option at the wing position by agreeing to acquire Peyton Watson in a trade involving the Denver Nuggets and other teams.

Watson and the Cavs also struck an agreement on a four-year, $88 million contract. ESPN first reported the news on Wednesday, Aug. 19. The Cavs will trade small forward Max Strus to the Los Angeles Clippers and an unprotected first-round draft pick to the Nuggets as part of the deal.

The move for Watson comes after Akron native James announced on July 24 he would sign with the Philadelphia 76ers instead of his other top suitors, the Cavs, Miami Heat and Golden State Warriors.

A first-round pick (No. 30 overall) in the 2022 NBA Draft, Watson became a restricted free agent this offseason. As a rookie, he won the 2023 NBA title with the Nikola Jokic-led Nuggets.

Watson, 23, has spent all four of his NBA seasons in Denver.

NBA free agency: Were LeBron James, Rich Paul hinting at 76ers decision all along?

The Cavs landed on Watson after falling short in the James derby and losing Dean Wade earlier in free agency. Wade, who started 14 of Cleveland's 18 playoff games at small forward this past spring, also went to Philadelphia (four years, $39 million).

The Cavs telegraphed another move on Aug. 14, when they increased their financial flexibility by sending Dennis Schroder to the Charlotte Hornets for Tre Mann in a swap of backup point guards. The Cavs also gave the Hornets cash considerations, hard capping Cleveland at the second apron.

The deal involving Watson will be a five-team trade, NBA Insider for NBA on Prime Chris Haynes reported.

Listed as 6 feet, 8 inches and 200 pounds, Watson averaged 14.6 points on 49.1% shooting from the field (41.1% on 3-pointers), 4.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 29.6 minutes during the 2025-26 regular season. Watson missed 25 of the final 30 regular-season games and did not appear in the 2026 playoffs, with the Nuggets citing a hamstring injury. He started 40 of the 54 games in which he appeared.

Watson's career regular-season averages are 8.7 points on 47.9% shooting from the floor (36.1% on 3s), 3.5 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 21.9 minutes. His career playoff averages are three points on 36.4% shooting from the field (33.3% on 3s), 2.1 rebounds and 10.4 minutes.

title: Hornets guard Sion James discusses Charlotte's offseason additions

However, given their recent success, which includes a 25-win improvement from a season ago, there's great reason to trust general manager Jeff Peterson and the front office, at least that's what Hornets guard Sion James thinks. "We trust Jeff Peterson and the front office to do what they got to do. Excited to have Naz Reid, Grayson Allen, Royce O'Neale, all these guys that are joining us," said James.

"It's the nature of the business, and the reason we all play is to get better and to improve and to win a championship. The front office is just doing what they're supposed to be doing."

title: MRI reveals 'best-case scenario' for Dodgers closer Edwin Díaz
description: The imaging Dodgers closer Edwin Díaz underwent Wednesday was clean, manager Dave Roberts said. Díaz is on the IL with neck inflammation.
fullText:
The imaging Dodgers closer Edwin Díaz underwent in Los Angeles on Wednesday morning revealed a "best-case scenario," manager Dave Roberts said before the series finale against the Rockies.

"There were no findings, so that was good," Roberts said. "MRI was clean. It doesn't change the fact that he had this sensation in his neck. But I think to keep working on it, give it some rest as far as throwing the baseball."

Díaz officially went on the IL for "neck inflammation," but early theories on the injury, before he went to a specialist on Wednesday, suggested the issue could be related to the area around the trapezius, according to a person with knowledge of the situation.

Roberts said Wednesday that the results suggested the injury was more muscular, rather than nerve related.

"I think he'd been feeling the tightness in his neck," Roberts said. "But I think where it went to the other night, he hadn't felt that sensation. So that's what really checked him up."

Roberts said he didn't know exactly how long Díaz would be shut down from throwing, but he estimated that it probably would be only a couple of days.

The bullpen shuffle continued Wednesday, when the Dodgers activated right-hander Brock Stewart (right shoulder discomfort) from the 15-day IL. In a corresponding move, they designated right-hander Jonathan Hernández for assignment.

title: NC State, UNC to meet in inaugural 'Tobacco Road Classic' in Greensboro in December
description: One of college basketball's oldest rivalries is getting a new touch.
fullText:
One of college basketball's oldest rivalries is getting a new touch.

The University of North Carolina and NC State University announced their men's basketball programs will meet in the inaugural 'Tobacco Road Classic', a non-conference, neutral-site game to be held at First Horizon Coliseum in Greensboro.

"For the fans, it's a fun rivalry," said NC State head coach Justin Gainey. "I look forward to (as we lead up to that game) talking to our guys about the history of the tradition, and all the great coaches and players that have played in that rivalry."

The 2025-25 season was the first time since 1919 that long-time rivals did not play twice in the regular season. Because of league expansion, the ACC reduced its league schedule from 20 games to 18, which in turn forced the ACC to assign each school one "primary partner" to play home and away.

For UNC, that was Duke, and for NC State, that was Wake Forest. But the creation of this new event guarantees two of the state's most proud programs will meet twice in the regular season this year and next.

"The landscape is changing, but we have to make sure as caretakers of this game that we're finding ways to give back to the fans and give them what they want," said UNC head coach Michael Malone.

"UNC-NC State is one of the greatest rivalries in college basketball, and we're thrilled to bring it to Greensboro," said Scott Johnson, General Manager of First Horizon Coliseum.

"The Tobacco Road Classic gives fans the opportunity to experience this historic matchup in a neutral-site setting, and we're grateful to the universities, athletic directors, and coaches for making this game possible."

Tickets go on sale on Thursday, September 10th at Ticketmaster.com and the First Horizon Coliseum Ticket Office.

The December 15th game will mark the first time UNC and NC State will play in Greensboro in the regular season since they met in the Big 4 Tournament on November 30th, 1979.

title: A former Packers cornerback signs with Super Bowl champion Seahawks
description: Former All-Pro cornerback Trevon Diggs, who played briefly for the Packers late last season, has a new team.
fullText:
Trevon Diggs' arrival to the Green Bay Packers late last season was a low risk move but it still was met with some fanfare.

After all, he was a former All-Pro cornerback and viewed not too long ago as one of the game's best defensive backs. When the Packers signed him ahead of the team's Week 18 game, which ultimately was done as insurance following injuries to its defense, it formed a reunion between Diggs and Micah Parsons from their days together with the Dallas Cowboys.

"We're back," Parsons tweeted at the time.

But the two weren't back together on the field since Parsons was out for the year with a torn ACL injury that he suffered a couple weeks earlier.

And the reunion between the two friends within the organization was brief. The Packers chose not to re-sign the free agent Diggs in the offseason as they looked elsewhere to restock the position with the free agent signing of Benjamin St-Juste and the selection of second-round pick Brandon Cisse in the 2026 NFL Draft.

Diggs had remained a free agent as well until Wednesday, Aug. 19.

With two weeks remaining in training camp and three weeks before the new season kicks off, the 27-year-old has signed with the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks.

The team announced the signing on Wednesday, Aug. 19. Diggs' new contract is for one year, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Diggs will join a unit that propelled the Seahawks to a Super Bowl victory.

The Seahawks had the sixth-ranked defense in 2025, including the top-ranked scoring defense, third-ranked run defense and 10th-ranked passing defense.

Diggs' stint with the Packers in 2025 was brief.

He played in only two games and his impact and time on the field was minimal. He had two tackles in the Packers' 16-3 Week 18 loss to the Minnesota Vikings on Jan. 4. A majority of the Packers' starters sat in the regular season finale with their playoff position secured ahead of the game.

Diggs then had one tackle in the Packers' 31-27 wild-card playoff loss to the Chicago Bears on Jan. 10.

The Packers signed Diggs on Dec. 31 a day after his release from the Cowboys with cornerback Nate Hobbs lost for the year due to injury.

The Seahawks will hope they can get the player Diggs used to be earlier in his career. In his second NFL season, Diggs led the league and set a Cowboys record with 11 interceptions in 2021. He earned first-team All-Pro recognition.

He had a second Pro Bowl season in 2022.

In his first three seasons in the NFL, he played in 45 games.

But he has played in only 22 games over the last three seasons.

An assortment of injuries have hampered Diggs. A torn ACL limited Diggs to only two games in 2023. After playing in 11 in 2024, Diggs saw the field only eight times for the Cowboys in 2025. They released him following Week 17.

In 67 games in his career, Diggs has 242 tackles, 63 passes defended and 20 interceptions with more than half coming in one season.

This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: A former Packers cornerback signs with Super Bowl champion Seahawks

title: Rolly Romero opens up on 'dark place' before Ryan Garcia upset, says boxing 'almost tore me apart'
description: Romero enters Saturday's WBA title defense against friend Teofimo Lopez as a man worlds removed from the one who stepped into Times Square to face Ryan Garcia last year.
fullText:
Rolando "Rolly" Romero cringes at the thought. The 30-year-old WBA welterweight world champion won his belt when he did something many thought he was incapable of, upsetting Ryan Garcia in May 2025. Romero has not fought since then, and was waiting, and waiting, and waiting for a chance to defend the WBA title.

Now, he finds himself "stuck," like anyone would feel when tasked with fighting a friend, as Romero is with his buddy, former two-division champion Teofimo Lopez Jr. The pair of eccentric boxing personalities will clash this Saturday at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas on a PBC pay-per-view broadcast (8 p.m. ET / 5 p.m. PT).

Only the colorful banter that usually engulfs one of their fights will be missing this time.

"Everyone else ducked me, so now I'm stuck fighting my friend," said Romero, referring to Lopez, in an exclusive interview with Uncrowned. "Trust me, I didn't want to fight my friend. It was not on my list, but it is something that I have to do. We do have a history though."

Romero (17-2, 13 KOs) even has it down to the specific dates he and Lopez sparred.

The first time they met was May 23, 2015, at a boxing party. The first time they sparred was February 18, 2016, Romero recalled, when the pair were in their early 20s. Romero was getting Lopez ready for the 2016 Olympics. Lopez (22-2, 13 KOs) and his father and trainer, Teofimo Lopez Sr., traveled out to Las Vegas, to the gym where Romero worked out, and the two went at it.

Romero said that they both had their moments. It was that way in all their sessions, he said — a little of Lopez being up, followed by Romero coming back at him.

"I remember what attracted me to Teo, he was his usual self, and he said something out of pocket that I won't repeat here, but it was really funny and it was offbeat, but not with the intention of hurting anyone," Romero said. "I was able to relate to that, because to a degree, that is me. I mean everything pretty much what I say. If I call someone 'ugly,' it means they're ugly."

The second time they sparred was in October 2016, the third time in June 2017 and the last time was in October 2017.

"I love Teo, but once this fight was made, I decided to go [for it], because everyone else has been ducking me," Romero said. "This is going to be a hell of a fight, but every time I fight, it is a hell of a fight. I wanted to fight after beating Garcia. It wasn't injuries [keeping me out], it wasn't politics. It was everyone ducking me. Garcia ducked me for the rematch. Conor Benn ducked me. [Manny] Pacquaio ducked me. They all ducked me. It's why I didn't get into the ring sooner, although the time off benefitted me."

At that, Romero stepped back and brought up a resonating moment of his career. It was actually minutes before he stepped into the ring with Garcia, who was one of the headliners on Turki Alalshikh's ambitious Times Square fight card.

Romero, a major underdog at -1000 odds on some sportsbooks, stole the show that night, knocking down Garcia with a left hook in the second round. Romero sat on that momentum and rode out a unanimous victory. Yet around that same time, he also found himself feeling "stuck" again, leading into the signature victory of his career.

"I was in a bad place for a time there," he admitted. "I started doing some things I thought I would never do. I have a lot from my childhood that I carry with me, but if you notice, when I got in that classic car in Times Square, heading a few feet over to fight [Garcia], if you notice my eyes, I was gone, lost. I had to kill myself [metaphorically]. It was a hard change. I suffered throughout that down time. I had to kill myself, because I was in a dark place. It's not that I did not like myself, but I had to change.

"I had to find the right way to live my life, because I was living my life like a wild animal. I'm not saying I was doing drugs or cocaine, but I had no right to punch every random person in the face just because I liked doing it. It's not a good way to live. It's just an analogy — I didn't actually do that. But you have to live your life with integrity, and I wasn't living like that.

"Look back at me in that car just before the Garcia fight. No one knows this, but I never beat Ryan Garcia. If it was me, I would have knocked Ryan Garcia out cold that night. I take no part in what happened in that fight. It had nothing to do with me. I know for a fact it was not me."

Romero said it was instead "God" who imbued him with a wisdom he felt before the Garcia fight. He stressed he felt possessed by God before he stepped into the ring.

"When they had us drive to the ring in these cars, God's voice was echoing so loudly in my head that I couldn't hear anyone, it was like I wasn't there," Romero recalled. "I didn't know where I was, or what I was about to do. It's why I had that blank stare on my face driving to the ring. I wasn't there. It was like getting hit by a thunderbolt and I didn't burn. I looked off in the car because I heard God's voice."

It's "God's voice" that Romero hopes will guide him again against Lopez. He was giving away backpacks to his former elementary school when he spoke to Uncrowned. It brought back memories of him getting in constant trouble in school. He could not clearly speak until he was 12.

"It's why I genuinely believe that I'm on some kind of spectrum," he said. "I suppose it's why I can remember specific dates and why I fight. This fight is going to be fun. I know Teo is a good dancer, and I think people are starting to realize that I am a lot smarter than they realize.

"Anything can happen in this fight, and I can't really say what I am going to do and what [Lopez] is going to do. I am settled in my life. Boxing can tear you apart. I know, it almost tore me apart. It's taken awhile, but I have found contentment. I know God is with me no matter what. God will deliver me to where I have to go. It's based on faith and trust. When I fought [Gervonta] 'Tank' Davis, I wasn't ready for that fame or money. When I heard God's true voice [before the Garcia fight], that truly changed me."

title: Deion Sanders served subpoena for son's bankruptcy trial. Can he avoid testifying?
description: Can Deion Sanders get out of a subpoena? Colorado coach faces trial conflict during opening week of Buffaloes football season.
fullText:
An attorney for Colorado football coach Deion Sanders has accepted service of a subpoena for Sanders to testify at his son Shilo's bankruptcy trial in Denver the same week Colorado opens the season at Georgia Tech on Sept. 3, according to new court filing on Aug. 19.

The court filing said Deion Sanders' attorney, Harvey Steinberg, agreed to accept service of the subpoena recently on behalf of his client via email. The subpoena commands Deion Sanders to appear at the trial, which begins Aug. 31 and is scheduled to last approximately five days through Sept. 4. The Colorado football team is scheduled to leave for Georgia on Sept. 1.

Sanders' attorney now could try to stop the subpoena by filing a motion to quash it. But it would be up to the judge in the case, Michael Romero, who previously acknowledged the conflict with Colorado's season-opening week.

"The subpoena commands attendance within 100 miles of where Mr. Sanders resides, is employed, and regularly transacts business in person," said the proof of service filed in court Aug. 19.

Shilo Sanders, 26, filed for bankruptcy in 2023 with more than $11 million in debt. He owes almost all of it to a former security guard at his school in Dallas, John Darjean, who sued him and accused him of causing him permanent injuries in 2015 when he tried to confiscate his phone at school at his father's request. Darjean won a $11.89 million default judgment in the case in 2022 after Shilo Sanders didn't show up at trial.

A scheduling conflict with a job or a football game won't be enough to quash the subpoena, according to one legal expert contacted by USA TODAY Sports. Sometimes a judge will quash a subpoena for other reasons such as undue burden or expense for the witness. Romero previously noted Deion Sanders might have relevant testimony to provide in the trial, where Shilo Sanders is trying to free himself of the debt.

"I'm not sure why a judge would agree that a person needing to go to work is a good reason to quash (a subpoena)," said Mechele Dickerson, a law professor at the University of Texas. "Lots of witnesses have jobs so if `I'd have to miss work' is a defense, almost all involuntary witnesses could avoid testifying."

A message seeking comment from Steinberg wasn't immediately returned. Darjean's attorney, Ori Raphael, offered to schedule Sanders' testimony at a scheduled time, according to an email attached to the proof of service.

"Happy to discuss arrangements to set a defined scheduled window for his testimony," said the email from Raphael to Sanders' attorney.

The subpoena comes at the request of Darjean's attorney, who filed the proof of service for the subpoena Aug. 19. The Boulder County Sheriff's Office previously attempted to serve Sanders with the subpoena on the Boulder campus Aug. 11, but was told Sanders was not available to receive it during a preseason practice.

"Unable to gain access into secure area of CU," the sheriff's deputy noted afterward, according to the new court filing.

The sheriff's office noted it is common for civil service to require multiple attempts.

"While coordinating with university staff to identify a time for service, our office was contacted by Mr. Sanders' legal counsel, who indicated they were able to accept the documents on his behalf," the Boulder sheriff's office told USA TODAY Sports on Aug. 18. "Because his counsel was located outside Boulder County, we transferred the paperwork to the appropriate jurisdiction for service."

The issue at trial is whether the debt stems from a willful and malicious injury. Darjean is fighting to collect on the judgment and argues that because it stems from a willful and malicious injury, he is not allowed to discharge it under bankruptcy law. Shilo Sanders has said he acted in self-defense and therefore should be entitled to discharge the debt because it was not willful and malicious.

title: The epic blockbuster that could be India's answer to The Odyssey
description: The Ramayana is one of India's most famous stories – and now the heroic epic has been adapted into two mega-budget films that the team behind it are hoping will be a global event.
fullText:
The Ramayana is one of India's most famous stories – and now the heroic epic has been adapted into two mega-budget films that the team behind it are hoping will be a global event.

This year, amid the hit superhero movies and kids' animations, an adaptation of an ancient poem involving mythical beasts, almighty gods and a hero toting a bow and arrow has been a smash at the box office: Christopher Nolan's stirring take on Homer's Odyssey.

But it may not be the only many-thousand-year-old epic verse to become a big-screen sensation this year. That's, at least, what the team behind a new two-part adaptation of Hindu poem the Ramayana will be hoping. The first part is set to be released globally in November, to coincide with the Hindu Diwali festival, and it's been produced on a budget that is unprecedented for an Indian film.

The Ramayana is believed to have been written around the 4BC by Valmiki, a poet and maharishi who composed nearly 24,000 shlokas (verses) telling the tale. It centres on Rama, a prince and avatar of the Hindu god of preservation Vishnu, whose wife Sita is kidnapped by the wicked king Ravana, leaving Rama with the task of rescuing her.

The story has been adapted many times before, and more than two billion people around the world are thought to be familiar with it. But it has never been told on quite such a scale as this. Sony Pictures recently came on board as international distributors. A-list Indian film stars Ranbir Kapoor (Rama) and Yash (Ravana) are in leading roles. Hollywood composers Hans Zimmer and AR Rahman are on the soundtrack.

And a reported $200 to 250 million (£147.5m to £184m) has been spent on Ramayana, with a similar budget attached to its sequel (due to be released in November 2027). That makes them both easily the most expensive Indian films ever made, way more than the $68 million (£50m) spent on the next most expensive film, 2024's Kalki 2898 AD. The total amount spent on the two forthcoming Ramayana films is double the combined budget of Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows Part 1 and 2, and not far below that of the entire Hobbit trilogy ($623m or £460m).

The film's producer and mastermind Namit Malhotra talks about Ramayana as a global event, aimed at audiences everywhere. "This was always conceived to be for the world," he tells the BBC. "From India, for the world."

As evidenced by the titles in the trailer and on all the posters for the first film, this is "Namit Malhotra's Ramayana", a visually splendid epic that places Malhotra's expertise in visual effects front and centre. The son of a Bollywood producer and grandson of a cinematographer, Malhotra started a VFX company – now known as Double Negative, or DNEG – in his dad's garage in Mumbai aged 19. The company has since worked on many films – including Blade Runner 2049, Oppenheimer, all three Dune films, and, yes, The Odyssey itself – and won a total of eight Oscars.

Malhotra's name is on the posters, but the acclaimed Nitesh Tiwari is Ramayana's director. He notes the recent success of Indian cinema worldwide, citing such films as 2022's global action movie hit RRR (which took $145m/£107m at the global box office) and 2023's crime drama Animal ($95m/£70m). "More Indian films have started to find acceptance with audiences globally," he says. "This has encouraged our film-makers to aim bigger, because the potential return on a film is no longer restricted primarily to the Indian box office."

The Ramayana story may be new to some western audiences, but its ubiquity in India is hard to overstate. "The stories of Ramayana have been told by every grandmother to their grandkid," says Malhotra. "It's like when you learn about Santa Claus or Jesus Christ."

"It's not just Hindu families," says Rajinder Dudrah, professor of Cultural Studies and the Creative Industries at Birmingham City University in the UK and author of several books on Indian cinema. "I think anybody who's grown up on Indian popular culture – Indians primarily, but also South Asians across the board, Bengalis, Pakistanis – will have watched variations of films which take root in the Ramayana story."

Adaptations of the Ramayana stretch from the 9th-Century Javanese poem Kakavin Ramayana and 12th-Century Tamil interpretation Ramavataram to the 1992 Indo-Japanese anime Ramayana: The Legend of Prince Rama. The 2008 American animation Sita Sings the Blues tells the story from the perspective of Rama's kidnapped princess, while 2010's Raavan challenges the image of the kidnapper as a villain and 2022's RRR places the story in the era of Britain's colonial rule over India.

• 12 of the best films of 2026 so far

• Five things you need to know about The Odyssey

• The 'real Indiana Jones' who found an ancient 'lost' city

In modern India, the most commonly known iteration is the TV series Ramayan (1987-88). "The whole country came to a standstill when the TV show ran in the 80s," says Malhotra. "As children, we would sit in front of the television every Sunday, waiting for it to start."

Although it originates from a Hindu text, Malhotra says that Ramayana transcends religion.

"I have always maintained that we are talking culture," he tells the BBC. "We're not talking religion. We're saying, listen: let's talk about the ideology. It's not anti- any nationality. It's not anti- any religion. It's not anti- any race. Because when you're talking about five or 10,000 years ago, nothing else existed. So there was no reason for the divide. The agenda of cinema is not to be divisive. It's to celebrate our differences and unify us."

"Ramayana is ultimately about moral values, relationships, and the emotions that come with them," believes Tiwari. "The biggest challenge was ensuring that those emotions were not overshadowed by the splendour of the world we were creating. However magnificent the world around the characters might be, the audience must remain emotionally connected to their journeys."

This adaptation of Ramayana may be contemplating some fundamental human beliefs and quandaries, but it's the dazzling special effects that will surely get fans into cinemas. One of DNEG's most impressive tricks on Ramayana is the creation of a kind of AI-assisted post-dubbing technology that makes the film's characters appear to be speaking in any given language. Unlike in dubbed films from the past, characters' lips will move perfectly in sync with the translated dialogue so the English, Spanish, and other versions of the film are completely seamless.

"We are at the forefront of creating new technology," says Malhotra. "We're trying to make sure that if English is your first language, you should watch it in your first language." He says he's not sure even at this stage how many languages the film will be available to watch in, but "if we pick English, Mandarin, Spanish and a few Indian languages, you've already covered five, six billion people on the planet".

Perhaps born from DNEG's work on Inception, Oppenheimer and The Odyssey, a rumour has circulated recently about Christopher Nolan's possible involvement in the editing of Ramayana. "I really wish it were true!" says Tiwari.

What's for sure is that Ramayana's ambition rivals that of any Nolan film. Its sequel, Ramayana 2, is shooting now. Malhotra mentions spin-off TV series, merchandise and more. What of his own ambition? Is he hoping for a cinematic empire that will make him the next George Lucas, Peter Jackson or Marvel creator Stan Lee?

"I don't think anyone, including Stan Lee, would have thought he's going to be who he is," Malhotra says."What I'm excited about is what we're doing right now, which is some of the oldest IP [intellectual property] in the world. This is not simply the beginning of a film. It is the beginning of a journey to celebrate India's cultural richness with the world."

Ramayana: Part 1 will be released internationally in November.

title: US warns of AI-powered attacks on Siemens PLCs in critical infrastructure
description: U.S. cybersecurity agencies warn that threat actors are using AI-generated scripts to exploit Siemens S7 Series programmable logic controllers (PLCs) in U.S. critical infrastructure.
fullText:
U.S. cybersecurity agencies warn that threat actors are using AI-generated scripts to exploit Siemens S7 Series programmable logic controllers (PLCs) in U.S. critical infrastructure.

PLCs are industrial computers used to automate and control machinery and physical processes in factories and other critical infrastructure.

The NSA, CISA, FBI, Department of Energy, and Environmental Protection Agency issued the joint advisory Wednesday, saying the attacks are ongoing.

"This advisory relates to an active threat to Siemens S7 Series programmable logic controllers (PLCs)," reads the advisory.

"However, ongoing PLC targeting activity is broader than Siemens PLCs. All PLC owners and operators should apply relevant mitigations to reduce the risk to their devices and systems."

The critical infrastructure sectors most targeted include Critical Manufacturing, Energy, Water and Wastewater Systems, Chemical, Food and Agriculture, and Commercial Facilities. The agencies also note that Siemens S7 PLCs are used in the Defense Industrial Base, which could also be targeted.

Threat actors are using internet scanning services, including Censys and ZoomEye, to find exposed Siemens PLCs and exploit critical and high-severity vulnerabilities, outdated software, and weak authentication.

The advisory says the attackers are using artificial intelligence to develop Python exploitation scripts that use the 'snap7.dll' and 'python-snap7' libraries to communicate with Siemens S7 PLC devices.

These custom tools are disguised as legitimate OT monitoring software and can provide read and write access to PLC memory, configuration data, and ladder logic programs over the S7comm protocol.

The agencies say the activity appears focused on persistent reconnaissance, potentially preparing attackers for disruption to critical infrastructure, including stealing sensitive data, damaging equipment, causing extended downtime, or leading to safety incidents.

The actively targeted devices include Siemens S7-200, S7-300, S7-400, S7-1200, and S7-1500 PLCs.

Organizations are urged to inventory Siemens S7 PLCs, install the latest security updates, block internet access, strengthen access controls, and monitor for unusual activity targeting these devices.

Today's advisory follows a recent increase in attacks targeting exposed PLCs at U.S. critical infrastructure organizations.

In July, hackers targeted more than 30 Minnesota water utilities, causing equipment malfunctions and forcing some facilities to switch to manual operations temporarily.

CISA later warned of an increase in attacks against internet-exposed PLCs used by water and wastewater utilities.

Earlier in April, U.S. agencies also warned that Iranian-linked hackers were targeting internet-exposed Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley PLCs, causing disruptions and financial loss across multiple critical infrastructure sectors.

title: Universality of Gradient Descent Neural Network Training
description: It has been observed that design choices of neural networks are often crucial for their successful optimization. In this article, we therefore discuss the question if it is always possible to redesign a neural network so that it trains well with gradient descent. This yields the following universality result: If, for a given network, there is any algorithm that can find good network weights for a classification task, then there exists an extension of this network that reproduces these weights and the corresponding forward output by mere gradient descent training. The construction is not intended for practical computations, but it provides some orientation on the possibilities of meta-learning and related approaches.

title: ADHD charity complains about Channel 4 documentary
description: One newspaper calls Channel 4’s The Great ADHD Myth? "the most controversial show of the year".
fullText:
An ADHD charity has said it has complained to media regulator Ofcom about a Channel 4 documentary that suggested the condition is a myth.

The programme, titled The Great ADHD Myth?, was broadcast on Tuesday and its host, NHS psychiatrist Dr Max Pemberton, concluded it was "a social construct, not a disorder of the brain".

ADHD UK filed a complaint, saying: "ADHD is not a myth. It is not a social construct."

The Royal College of Psychiatrists also warned against "invalidating the condition".

Channel 4 defended the show, saying there is "considerable public debate on various aspects of ADHD" and it "is legitimate for that debate to be explored and for conventional understandings to be challenged".

The programme featured experts who are sceptical about ADHD and the way it is treated.

It also followed a 10-year-old boy who stopped his medication and made lifestyle changes to see how it affected his behaviour. The documentary ended with his mother saying he would stay off the drugs for the time being.

A caption at the end of the programme said the boy went back on his medication two months after filming and his school performance improved, but that he wanted to come off them again in the future.

ADHD UK said: "The programme's own end credits told you what its 60 minutes wouldn't: the boy at its centre went back on his medication, and his schoolwork improved.

"Their experiment disproved their conclusion. They aired their version anyway. We have already complained to Ofcom."

There was also criticism from Prof Subodh Dave, president of the Royal College of Psychiatrists, who acknowledged that people "may have their own opinions about the diagnosis and treatment of ADHD", but said: "Invalidating the condition does a disservice to people with ADHD and professionals involved in their care."

He added: "The focus should be on improving access to high-quality assessments and care by addressing waiting lists that leave many people without vital support for years at a time, not questioning the legitimacy of a well-established neurodevelopmental disorder."

Another charity, ADHD Embrace, raised concerns with Channel 4 in advance, warning the programme risked "perpetuating misinformation about ADHD as a condition and discrimination against those families whose lives have been severely impacted by the condition".

In a statement, Channel 4 said: "This documentary does not deny the lived experience of those diagnosed with ADHD, but does present the view of an extensive range of senior medical experts - many of whom work or have worked with the NHS or have held presidential roles at professional membership bodies - who seek to question the conventional understanding of ADHD and if it is a neurodevelopmental condition.

"They also ask whether modern living has contributed to a rise in diagnoses, and whether there may be better alternatives for some children than medication."

The channel also said the programme sought to explore whether societal factors were contributing to the rise in diagnosis and medication, especially among boys.

Channel 4 said: "Whilst the film does not seek to provide answers from one family's experience, their experiences have opened up discussion around whether today's world is equipped to accommodate ADHD behaviours and the ethics of medicating these, particularly in children and particularly when the long-term effects remain unknown."

The Guardian called the programme "the most controversial show of the year", and its four-star review said the documentary "will incense and offend some of its viewers", but that "Pemberton answers his questions convincingly".

The Times also gave four stars, saying much of the documentary "felt convincing, or at least the start of a necessary discussion".

ADHD is described by the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (Nice) as "a behavioural syndrome characterised by hyperactivity, impulsivity, and inattention".

The NHS estimates that about 2.5 million people in England have ADHD, including those without a formal diagnosis.

Diagnosis rates of ADHD and autism have soared, and waiting lists for assessments on the NHS in England are at record levels, with lists even closing in some areas due to the huge demand.

Research from University College London suggests nearly a 20-fold increase in the number of UK adults diagnosed with ADHD between 2000 and 2018.

Despite these rises in diagnosis and referrals, some studies suggest ADHD is actually underdiagnosed.

In June, the Lancet Regional Health Europe journal published research suggesting that while around 1.2% of adults in England had an ADHD diagnosis, international prevalence data estimates it affects 3-5% of people. The authors of the study said this indicates it could still be under-diagnosed, particularly in older age groups.

title: Have you been Flocked? This website lets you find out
description: More than 4.6 million license plates appear in the website’s collection of public Flock records.
fullText:
People aren’t exactly thrilled about Flock’s growing surveillance network. Communities are canceling contracts, protesters are taking down cameras in increasingly creative ways, and activists have built a crowdsourced map showing where the devices are hiding in plain sight. Even Flock has announced new privacy restrictions as the backlash grows.

Now, drivers can search some of those records for themselves.

A website called Have I Been Flocked? lets you enter your license plate number and check whether it appears in publicly released records of searches conducted through Flock Safety’s system. As of Aug. 17, the website had compiled nearly 242 million searches involving more than 4.6 million plates.

The need for that kind of transparency isn’t hypothetical. A recent Washington Post investigation found that at least 50 law enforcement officers had been charged with or accused of misusing license plate readers, including to stalk women without their knowledge or consent.

The concerns extend beyond individual officers. Public records reviewed by 404 Media documented more than 4,000 Flock searches conducted by local and state police at the request of federal officials, as informal favors, or for potentially immigration-related purposes. Flock says ICE cannot directly access its system, but the records show how local agencies can search the network on the federal government’s behalf.

Have I Been Flocked? won’t reveal everything Flock knows about your car, and finding a match doesn’t necessarily mean you were investigated. Nevertheless, here's how to run a search — and understand what the results actually mean.

Go to HaveIBeenFlocked.com, enter your license plate number in the search box, and click “Search.”

If your plate appears in the database, the results may include when it was searched, the agency associated with the query, the person who conducted it, and the reason provided for looking up the plate. Some of that information may be incomplete or redacted.

The website is part of Footnote4a, an independent editorial project focused on mass surveillance and government contracts. Its database is built from Flock audit logs released by local governments through transparency portals or obtained through public records requests.

Those audit logs document searches made within Flock’s system. According to the website's FAQ, the license plate and stated reason shown in the results are information that a Flock operator manually entered.

A match means a Flock user queried the company’s database for that license plate. It does not necessarily mean that your car was stopped, that you were suspected of committing a crime, or that you were formally investigated.

The person conducting the search may have been a police officer, but the website notes that not every Flock user is a member of law enforcement. Businesses, schools, homeowners associations, and other private organizations also use Flock’s technology.

The reason listed alongside a result may provide more context. An operator could say the search was related to a stolen vehicle, traffic stop, missing person, or another investigation. However, because users supply those explanations themselves, they should not be treated as an independent account of what happened.

The website also does not show whether the search produced a match inside Flock’s system or reveal exactly what the operator saw.

Have I Been Flocked? has collected hundreds of millions of records, but its database is still incomplete.

The project depends on public records released by individual government agencies, and relatively few make their complete Flock audit logs easily available. The records that are released can also be heavily redacted or out of date.

"There can be a significant delay — months or even years — between when a search occurs and when it appears on this website," the project explains on its site.

That means an empty result does not prove that nobody has ever searched for your plate; it only means the number does not appear in the website's current records.

Operator names can also be incomplete. Flock’s audit logs often shorten an operator’s name to a first initial and the first three letters of a surname — turning a name such as Kevin Zachary into "K. Zac" (an example provided by HaveIBeenFlocked.com). That can make it difficult to determine exactly who performed a search. The website compares these partial names with public police rosters and employment records to identify a likely match, but warns that the results are not definitive.

Have I Been Flocked? also attempts to match those partial names with public employment records, but warns that its identifications are probabilistic and should be independently verified.

If you find a search that concerns you, the project recommends filing a public records request with the agency linked to it. It also advises anyone who believes they were subjected to improper surveillance to speak with an attorney.

The plate lookup is only one part of the website — visitors can also browse searches by agency and explore reports involving immigration enforcement, First Amendment activity, low-level offenses, noncriminal activity, and searches apparently intended to "develop probable cause." After years of drivers being kept in the dark, the website makes at least some of Flock’s surveillance visible.

title: The Steam Revenue Report
description: Estimated earnings for every game on Steam. Constantly updated, free, and every number is clickable.
fullText:
Every paid game on Steam with at least one review, as one dot. Time runs left to right;
 estimated lifetime earnings run bottom to top on a logarithmic scale. Colour is the game's
 review score. Hover for a name, click to open its page.

How concentrated is the money? The curve below plots the share of games against the share
 of revenue they account for. The straight diagonal is what perfect equality would look like.

0 would mean every game earns the same; 1 would mean one game earns everything.
 For comparison, national income Gini coefficients run from about 0.25 to 0.63.
 Check out the Blue Ocean Games piece on this topic
 here.

Worth noting a limitation of the reviews → revenue method:
 8,768 paid games have no reviews at all.
 Too few sales to measure, not necessarily zero sales.

Every paid game, sorted into earnings bands. The counts shift when you change the Boxleiter multiplier (see way above), as the bands are dollar amounts and the estimates move underneath them.

Steam's catalogue grew faster than its revenue. These three charts show what that did to
 an individual game's prospects.

Each year as 100%, split across the earnings tiers. This is the answer to
 “were a new game's odds better in 2016 than in 2025?” Click any segment to browse
 the games in it.

Median and top-decile earnings for the biggest genres. A game counts towards a genre only
 when the tag is one of its six most popular tags — so “roguelike economics” here
 describes games that are roguelikes, not games that merely carry the tag somewhere
 down the list.

The same 30 genres, but year by year. Each cell is that genre's median earnings for games
 released that year, divided by the median for every game released that year. Above
 1.0 the genre beat the market; below it, it lost.

Dividing by the same year's market makes this (potentially) useful across time.
 A ratio compares a genre against its own contemporaries, and both halves have had the same
 number of years to gather reviews, so the accrual bias divides out.

The same ratio one year at a time, against how many games shipped into that genre. Press play
 on the timeline below the chart to watch the years run.

What a game charges, and what it earns. Bands are half-open and aligned to Steam's
 .99 price points, so nothing is counted twice.

The twenty-five highest estimates on Steam. Estimates are least reliable at this end of the
 curve: review rates vary a great deal between mega-hits, and a percentage point of drift
 here is worth hundreds of millions of dollars.

This method of revenue estimation has blind spots! They're listed here rather than in a footnote, because a number is only useful if you know what it excludes.

18,385 free games are in the catalogue, but are
 estimated. Counter-Strike, Dota, Warframe and Path of Exile (some of the platform's biggest games)
 earn money through items and
 battle passes, and none of that is visible to a method built on price × reviews.

10,693 games in the catalogue are delisted or carry no
 published price. We can't estimate them, but can't count them as free, so they're
 counted separately and left out of every dollar figure.

8,768 paid games have zero reviews. The method
 returns $0.00 for them, which is likely slightly low; we'd expect actual estimated gross revenue to be between
 $0 and $750.

We multiply by a game's current list price. Most games launch high and discount for
 years afterwards, so lifetime revenue accrues at a mix of prices this method never
 sees. Long-lived games with heavy discount histories are overstated.

The price we use is the US list price. Steam sells worldwide at regionally adjusted
 prices, often far lower, and the mix varies enormously by genre and audience.

Add-on content and bundle sales aren't included. And the share of buyers who leave a
 review has changed over Steam's lifetime, which means one multiplier applied across
 20+ years of releases is a simplification.

Valve doesn't publish sales figures. It does publish review counts, and a game's reviews
 are roughly proportional to its sales, so multiplying reviews by a constant gives an
 estimated unit count. Multiply that by price and you have estimated gross revenue.

The approach is named for Mike Boxleiter, who first published the ratio from indie sales
 data. It has been revisited repeatedly since — Simon Carless at GameDiscoverCo and Jake
 Birkett among others have published refinements, and the credible range of the constant runs
 from roughly 20× to 60× depending on genre, price, era and audience. Cheap games
 bought impulsively tend to review at different rates from expensive ones bought deliberately.

We publish at 35× by default and let you move it, because a single number
 presented without a dial implies a precision this method doesn't have. Every dollar figure on
 this page is an estimate with a wide error bar, and it is most reliable in aggregate and
 least reliable for any single game.

Data refreshes continuously; the timestamp at the top of the page is the moment this build
 was made. Release dates before 1997 or in the future are treated as data errors and excluded.

title: Seven of the Most Common WhatsApp Scams (and How to Avoid Them)
description: WhatsApp scams thrive on human error—learn how to spot them and keep yourself safe.
fullText:
Most typical WhatsApp scams aren’t high-tech security breaches. They aren’t orchestrated by state-sponsored hacker groups with a bottomless wallet and military-grade technology. In fact, most of them are run by low-tech crime syndicates relying on social engineering techniques to take advantage of people’s blind spots and trust in others.

Meta removed 6.8 million WhatsApp accounts associated with cyber crime and digital scams just in the second half of 2025. But the attacks show no sign of slowing down because they are low on cost and easy to spin up, with chatbots executing most of the legwork on autopilot. However, there’s a flip side to all this: social engineering only works when you don’t know what to look for.

Most of these scams follow a specific playbook and have a similar pattern of execution. If you know what to watch out for, you can stop them before they compromise your data or lead you into a financial trap. Below are seven of the most common scams that WhatsApp cybercriminals like to run, with tips on how to safely avoid every one of them. Learn how to tell when you’re about to be scammed, enable new features that protect your account privacy, and know how to respond when an attack is already underway.

I’d rate this as the most dangerous WhatsApp scam in this list, because it locks you out of your entire account and puts it in the hands of the attacker. It’s also one of the simplest to execute. Here's how it works: A scammer enters your phone number on WhatsApp to log into your account using their device. This triggers WhatsApp to send a verification code to your registered phone number. Right on cue, someone pretending to be a friend or family member texts you with a request to share the verification code you just received under some false premise. If you hand over that verification code you received in response, that’s it: WhatsApp will log you out of your current device and transfer access of your account to the attacker, who can then do whatever they want with it, including changing all your credentials.

Avoiding this attack is also equally simple. Just don’t share your WhatsApp verification code to anyone over a call or text, even if it seems like someone from your contact list. If you receive a message from WhatsApp with a new verification code, take it as a sign that someone’s attempting to hijack your account and don’t just assume it’s a glitch.

Also make it a point to enable 2-step verification on your WhatsApp account as a standard practice, by navigating to Settings > Account > Two-step verification in the Android or iOS app. That way, an attacker with a stolen verification code won’t be able to get into your account right away, because they will also need to verify the request using your preferred authentication method.

Once an attacker has access to someone’s WhatsApp account, often by doing just as I discussed in the last example, they will fire off a string of messages using that compromised account to everyone in the victim’s contact list. They will pretend to be the victim in some kind of medical or financial emergency, then ask people to send them money as quickly as possible.

Citing an emergency creates panic within people, which makes them less likely to verify the authenticity of the request. By the time the original victim gets around to sharing that their account has been hijacked, multiple people have already been scammed using that stolen account. Scammers will sometimes even use AI-generated voice messages to make the request seem legitimate, provided they already know what the real account holder sounds like.

I always tell my friends and acquaintances never to transfer funds or honor a sensitive request sent over text without double-checking if it’s real. When you get a request like this on WhatsApp, simply call that person directly over the phone, using a known contact number that’s not been recently changed. If the requester claims that the number has changed or the phone is out of battery, that’s a red flag. If you’re worried that the request might be authentic, call someone else who lives near that person or go over physically to verify.

WhatsApp is a popular choice for online dating scams thanks to its popularity as a messaging service, but these scams rarely give themselves away at first. Instead, attacker spend months building rapport with a potential victim over long chains of text and audio messages. When they’re confident about the level of trust they have established, the asks begin. First, they ask for small transfers that don’t go over $100, citing something urgent but non-critical.

Slowly, the requests grow in financial value until the victim realizes something’s up and calls it off. Family emergencies, personal cash flow issues, and even investment offers in cryptocurrency or private funds are often used to pressure victims into giving away money. If someone you’ve never met in physical space asks you for cash, that’s an immediate giveaway that something is wrong. Normal people rarely ask someone for money unless they know them well in person, so use caution whenever you spot a request like that.

This is a very common play that’s especially popular when targeting demographics with low digital literacy. You receive a private message from what looks like an official WhatsApp account claiming that you’ve been invited to try out a new subscription tier that isn’t available to the general public. Often, the message is accompanied by a link to download and install an app from an unknown source. As soon as you click on the link, it installs malware on your device that could range from ransomware to keyloggers, which can then be used to execute blackmails or cyberattacks.

If you receive a message inviting you to WhatsApp Gold, WhatsApp Premium, or any other equivalent subscription tier that cannot be verified through official sources, do not click on the link. Also generally avoid installing apps that don’t come from official sources like Google Play or App Store, unless you explicitly trust the developer sending you the link. Apps installed from third-party links are not subject to the usual security audit that official marketplaces require them to clear, which increases the risk of being infected by malware. Most smartphones disable third-party app installation by default for this exact reason.

If you want to be even safer, navigate to Settings > Privacy > Advanced inside WhatsApp and toggle on Disable link previews. While link previews in WhatsApp are generally safe, they can expose your device’s metadata and general geolocation to the website administrator for a small period, which can be used to escalate more sophisticated cyber attacks.

A common pattern among WhatsApp scams is the use of official names and logos to impersonate service providers and trusted authorities, like banks, delivery services, tech support, and sometimes even local law enforcement. Since people are more likely to trust messages that come from these providers without further verification, it gives attackers the window they need to make otherwise unreasonable requests.

If someone claims to be a bank employee who needs you to share a one-time password for a security check, offer to call them back using a known official number instead of continuing the conversation in the same (potentially compromised) channel. Same goes for anyone who identifies as a local law enforcement or tax department official. They could threaten you with non-compliance if you refuse, but remember that you can always call the agency and verify it with them officially, instead of acting on a random call. Sometimes, scammers even pretend to be tech support and ask for remote access to your device so they can troubleshoot an issue. IT staff knows not to do this outside of established channels.

The problem with these requests is that they can vary wildly in how the attacker presents themselves and what their initial ask is. But the common thread is that organizations or their employees won’t typically call you from their personal number or even an unknown business number to ask for details. Just politely offer to call back using an official number that you can verify, then disconnect the call. That almost always stops these attempts right away, because they use a spray-and-pray approach to target large numbers of people and look for an easy mark. I’ve personally received multiple calls from people claiming to be local law enforcement reaching out about a passport address verification, but a quick call to the department landline showed that this wasn’t the case.

According to the FTC, people in the United States lost over $500 million in 2024 to job scams alone. With unemployment rates being as high as they are, most people don’t want to antagonize anyone coming to them with a job offer. Scammers know this and they count on it. It may start by getting a WhatsApp text from an unknown number with an easy remote work offer. Sometimes, they will even pay you small amounts to establish trust in return for simple jobs like boosting a product listing.

Eventually, they’ll ask you to deposit a significant amount of funds with them before you receive the next batch of tasks, for “verification purposes.” That’s when you can immediately tell that something is wrong. Most people know that employers will never ask you for payment just to give you work, but scammers can come up with clever reasoning to justify these odd requests. Sometimes, the ask isn’t for a money deposit at all. Instead job scammers will demand access to your device or even ask you to complete a short survey using a (malicious) link.

Your best bet for spotting job scams on WhatsApp is to never trust an unknown number with an offer of employment or even an interview. No matter how small the request, it may offer a way for them to compromise your device or gain access to your accounts. Simply ask them to communicate using an official company email address or landline. If they refuse, that’s a strong indication you're being targeted.

WhatsApp scams prey on people’s emotional vulnerabilities, which is why pretending to be a charity or disaster relief fund is a common way to trick people into sending money. Worse still, these messages often get forwarded from one victim to another without verification, creating a sense of implicit trust that is not earned but assumed. You can use platforms like Charity Navigator and CharityWatch to determine if a charity is real and obtain their official contact details for verification. Most legitimate charities do not solicit donations through WhatsApp, and even if one does, it’s better (and safer) to pay through an official method listed on their organization website anyway.

WhatsApp scammers often use real people’s likenesses to perpetuate scams. If you’re worried about your profile picture or identity being used to commit fraud, you can restrict your profile photo, about section, and activity status to Contacts only by navigating to Settings > Privacy.

Periodically check for any unauthorized devices connected to your account by going to Settings > Linked devices. If you’re not sure if a log in came from a device you own, you should log out of all active sessions just to be safe.

Under Settings > Privacy, you can choose to toggle on silence unknown callers to avoid being approached by scammers and attackers using numbers not in your contact list.

WhatsApp now offers optional usernames for those who don’t want their phone number to be publicly visible on their account. You can access this feature by going to Settings > Account > Username on your mobile app.

When you suspect that something is a scam, use the Report and block option to notify WhatsApp of the attempt so it can put the attacker’s account under review.

title: 10 Finder Hacks Every Mac User Should Know
description: There's more to Finder than just viewing and opening files.
fullText:
Finder is one of the Mac's most underappreciated apps. At first glance, it appears to be a simple app that displays your files, but there's a lot more to Finder than that. This is an app that Apple has refined over decades, with hidden features to explore and third-party apps to install. With these 10 Finder hacks, you'll be able to add many of its most powerful features to your daily workflow.

The left pane in the Finder app has quite a few shortcuts. You can think of these as bookmarks that let you access various files and folders. However, you can personalize this list to fit your workflow. To start, drag any item in Finder's sidebar to reorder the list, which includes sections such as "Favorites" or "Locations." You can also drag individual items in a section to prioritize folders you access frequently. The best feature is the ability to remove stuff you don't use. To try it out, click the Finder button in the menu bar at the top of your screen, and select Settings > Sidebar. Uncheck items you don't need, such as Recent Tags (a feature I never use on my Mac). You can also drag any folder to the Favorites section in the sidebar, which is a faster way to open folders you access frequently.

Whenever I use the search box in Finder, it defaults to showing all the results from my Mac. I prefer to view results from the currently open folder, which takes a lot less time than going through all my files. You can make this happen by going to Finder Settings > Advanced and selecting the drop-down menu under "When performing a search." Here, select Search the Current Folder. While you're at it, you can also try out the hidden advanced search mode in Finder to add multiple search filters. This makes it easier to find a specific file in a massive, unorganized folder. After you type a query, hit the "+" button below Finder's search bar to reveal these filters.

When you delete files, they're sent to the Trash on your Mac. This folder takes up storage space, which can quickly become a problem for those of us with base model MacBooks. You can solve this by automatically deleting those files after 30 days. Go to Finder Settings > Advanced, and enable "Remove items from Trash after 30 days."

When you unzip a compressed file, your Mac pastes the contents in a new folder, but it doesn't automatically delete the original archive. You can make it automatically delete these files to clean up the mess. For this, you can press Command-Space, search for Archive Utility, and open the app. Next, click the Archive Utility button in the menu bar, and head over to Settings. Click the drop-down menu next to "After expanding," and choose "move archive to Trash."

Quick Look is one of macOS' best features. It allows you to preview any file without actually opening it. However, this feature doesn't let you preview the contents of folders, which means that when you select a folder and press Spacebar, you'll only see the size of the folder and how many files it has. To fix this, you can use a plugin called Folder Preview ($1.99), which does allow you to preview the contents of folders. There's a better version of the app called Folder Preview Pro ($9.99), which lets you copy, paste, and even preview files from within a folder preview.

Those who switch from Windows to Mac will immediately miss the lack of an obvious cut-and-paste workflow for files. Your Mac does ship with this feature, but it's not easy to discover. You can first copy a file by pressing Command-C, or going to the Edit menu and selecting "Copy." Next, open a different folder, and press Command-Option-V to move it, as opposed to pasting it. You may also use the Edit menu and select "Move Item Here." In case this option doesn't show up there, you can right-click an empty space in the destination folder, and hold Option to reveal "Move Item Here."

Finder supports unique actions for each file type, so you can perform tasks without even opening a file. For instance, you can right-click any image in Finder, and select Quick Actions > Remove Background. This will create a new image file without the background present in the original. The Quick Actions menu shows multiple actions for some file types, so you should explore it to find other useful functions.

Finder's toolbar has a set of buttons that cover the most common functions users need, but there are more that may prove to be useful for some people. Right-click an empty space in the Finder toolbar, and click "Customize Toolbar" to reveal these options. For example, you can drag the "Path" button to the toolbar, and select Done. You can now click "Path" any time to see the full folder path of any location in Finder. Similarly, the AirDrop button lets you select files and instantly opens the AirDrop sharing menu, which otherwise takes three clicks.

If you're tired of the standard white or black backgrounds that Finder defaults to, you can change the background color or even replace it with a wallpaper of your choice. This feature only appears when you use the "Icons" view in Finder. To check it out, open any folder in Finder, and press Command-1 (or click "View" in the menu bar, and pick "as Icons") to switch to the Icons view. Now press Command-J (or View > Show View Options) to open a pop-up window. Under "Background," you can select "Color" to set a new background color, or "Picture" to add a wallpaper. Note that the wallpaper won't automatically scale to fit the window, so if you resize windows often, you'll be left with a blank white space at times.
